runClassification: single-run focal observation; not a throughput benchmark
measurement: historical schema 1 single run with asymmetric timers; navigation and runtime installation excluded

methodology.truth: declared visible DOM/ARIA postconditions described per case; no independent hidden oracle was used
methodology.timing: Historical asymmetry: Playwright timing included its precondition assertions; SnapDOM timing started only after its semantic find returned. Both then included action and postconditions.
methodology.bytes: UTF-8 serialized bytes; no token estimates
methodology.playwrightSuccessEvidence: expect() returned no serialized semantic evidence; ariaSnapshot() was explicitly requested and measured
methodology.playwrightFailureEvidence: deliberately wrong 150 ms expect() serialized matcher diagnostics; five of six contained an automatic ARIA snapshot
methodology.snapdomSuccessEvidence: authenticated daemon response including the structured assert and diff evidence
methodology.snapdomFailureEvidence: authenticated structured failure response for a deliberately absent exists predicate
methodology.comparabilityCaveat: The arms target the same user-visible effects, but some conjuncts/preconditions differ and the timer boundaries are asymmetric. SnapDOM's 15,035.8 ms total is 6.9% below Playwright's 16,155.4 ms total here, but that difference is not comparable and must not be presented as a speed advantage.
methodology.successEvidenceCaveat: Playwright's 0 B automatic-success field and explicit ariaSnapshot bytes measure separate calls, while SnapDOM bytes measure a richer automatic success envelope. Smaller/larger byte totals do not mean equivalent evidence.

isolation.direct: Playwright 1.62.1 and Chromium 151 installed under a throwaway temporary root; chromium.launch plus fresh non-persistent context
isolation.snapdom: repository product daemon with pinned runtime, OS-assigned port 55855 (not 8377), temporary token/logs and non-persistent contexts

cases.truth: The initially visible checkbox is absent and the page reports It's gone!.
cases.alignment: Same effect; Playwright also asserts the precondition, SnapDOM asserts a typed removal from its open baseline.

cases.truth: A visible checkbox is added back and the page reports It's back!.
cases.alignment: Same effect, different final text conjunct: Playwright checked It's back!; SnapDOM checked the checkbox accessible name A checkbox.

cases.truth: The disabled input becomes enabled and the page reports It's enabled!.
cases.alignment: Same effect; Playwright names disabled/enabled pre/postconditions, SnapDOM asserts a typed state diff plus final text.

cases.truth: The live Bootstrap dialog appears and its Woo-hoo paragraph is rendered without geometric occlusion.
cases.alignment: Same four claims; Playwright needed a custom elementFromPoint predicate for occlusion.

api: find Launch demo modal; click returned id

cases.truth: After Start, Hello World! is rendered after the asynchronous loading phase.
cases.alignment: Same effect; both arms used an explicit 10 second wait/retry budget.

cases.truth: After the delayed result has settled, a 300 ms wait produces no semantic change.
cases.alignment: Same effect; Playwright compares two explicit body ARIA snapshots, SnapDOM asserts changed:false against its baseline.

reproduction.networkSchema2DirectVersion: install the desired Playwright version outside the repository, then set VALUE_FOCAL_PLAYWRIGHT_ROOT to that temporary package root and run node experiment/value-focal.mjs --network
reproduction.schemaChange: The runner now emits schema 2: precondition/baseline outside both timers; target lookup, action and aligned postconditions inside both timers; add checks It's back! in both arms. It intentionally does not reproduce the unfair schema 1 timer.
reproduction.networkWarning: Public pages and timing vary. A new run must be stored as a new observation, not silently treated as identical to this committed run.
